chunks: And Zurarah narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said:
“Do not recite anything in the last two rakʿahs of the four obligatory rakʿah prayers, whether you are an Imam or not.”

He said: I said, “So what should I say in them?” He said: “If you are an Imam or by yourself, then say: ‘Subḥān Allāh, wa al-ḥamdu lillāh, wa lā ilāha illā Allāh’ three times, completing it as nine tasbīḥāt. Then say the takbīr and bow.”

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ: the final two units of prayer
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: the declaration that there is no god but Allah

ai.seo_question: What should be recited in the last two rakʿahs of the four obligatory prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for the final two rakʿahs of the four obligatory prayers, instructing that Qur'anic recitation is not to be done in them. Instead, the person praying as Imam or alone should recite prescribed tasbīḥ phrases three times before proceeding to takbīr and rukuʿ.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1159 – Zurarah narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) that He said:
"Do not recite anything (from the Qur'an) in the last two rak'ahs of the four obligatory rak'ah prayers, whether you are an Imam or not."

I (Zurarah) asked: "So what should I say in them?"
Imam (as) said: "If you are an Imam or praying alone, say: 'Subhan Allah (swt) (Glory be to Allah (swt)), Alhamdulillah (Praise be to Allah (swt)), and La ilaha illAllah (swt) (There is no god but Allah (swt))' three times, making a total of nine glorifications. Then say the takbir and bow (for ruku')."
